From: Lena Hoffman <lena@finteras.com>

Subject: Follow-up: performance/latency targets and regional routing

Thanks again for the call this morning — good to meet the team. Quick recap and a few clarifications so we can move to a technical deep-dive: 

- Target latency expectations: p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 250ms (for short prompts ~150 tokens). We also care about p99 spikes — please indicate fallbacks.
- Throughput/concurrency: we expect ~450 QPS peak across accounts, with the bulk in US (approx 60%), EU (30%), APAC (10%). Concurrency per user session ~4-8 outstanding requests.
- Streaming: for conversational product we need partial streaming (token-level) with time-to-first-byte < 50ms goal.
- Data residency: EU customer data must remain within EU region (no outbound KV cache replication), and logs containing PII must be retained in-fin for 90 days. 

Can you confirm which model variants you recommend, SLOs you can commit to by region, and whether the KV/prefix cache will respect EU-only residency? Also attaching the call recording and a small perf sampling spreadsheet.

Attachments: finteras-call-recording.mp3, perf_sample_v1.csv

—Lena
Security contact: sec-ops@finteras.com

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Cc: dylan_brooks@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: performance/latency targets and regional routing

Hi Lena — thanks for the clear summary. Appreciated the traffic split and latency targets. High level answers below; we'll cover details in the deep-dive.

- Latency & fallbacks: For the short prompt profile you described we recommend our 8-bit quantized Kestrel variant for production (p50 ~ 55-70ms US, p95 ~ 180-240ms US on c7g-backed pods); EU figures increase ~10-20ms depending on region availability. For p99 spikes we provide automatic fallback routing to a dedicated lower-latency hot pool and can enable token-level graceful degradation (emit partial streaming + reduce model steps) — we log and surface regressions in Console.

- Throughput/concurrency: We can provision reserved concurrency pools by region. For your 450 QPS peak with your proposed split, a starting allocation would be US: 275 QPS, EU: 135 QPS, APAC: 40 QPS with burst headroom. Concurrent user sessions of 4-8 are fine; we recommend request-level concurrency limits per API key to protect tail latency.

- Streaming: We support chunked streaming with time-to-first-byte optimizations (prefix caching + low-latency kernels). For the time-to-first-byte <50ms goal we'll need to validate on your realistic prompt lengths in the deep-dive; prelim numbers look achievable in US/EU where we have warm caches.

- Data residency & cache: KV/prefix cache can be constrained to region-scoped caches (EU-only) — no off-region replication for keys marked as EU-resident. Logs with PII can be configured to encrypt and store in customer-controlled S3/HSM in region; retention policy adjustable (we support 90d retention). We'll share SOC2/attestation docs in the next message.

Next steps:
1) Tech deep-dive (30–45 min) to validate sample payloads and run a small spike — propose Wed 11/11 or Thu 11/12 (US morning).
2) We'll prepare a perf eligibility matrix (per-region p50/p95/p99 and concurrency guidance) and a pre-demo checklist — attaching our Redwood performance playbook as a starter.
3) Please confirm traffic split and any special network egress/VPN requirements.

Attachments: redwood_perf_playbook.pdf

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Redwood Inference — Production-first inference

Hi Lena — Dylan here (infra/product). Quick answers and the proposed next steps from our side: 

- SOC2 & compliance: attaching the SOC2 summary and contact for our Security team. We can provide the full SOC2 Type II under an NDA/LoA; procurement typically signs our standard NDA and we exchange the artifact via secure share.

- Cache isolation: region-scoped caches are fully isolated at runtime (no async replication). We also offer a "no-analytics" mode that stops ORC-style telemetry exports for specified namespaces.

- SLA: For Dedicated customers we commit to 99.9% availability and p99 latency SLOs tailored per model/region in the contract; hosted customers receive best-effort p99 guidance and operational credits for sustained regressions. We will surface the concrete numbers in the procurement bundle.

Action items: 
1) Set 30–45 min technical deep-dive: Wed 11/11 09:00–09:45 PT or Thu 11/12 08:00–08:45 PT. Please confirm which works.
2) We'll run a 2-hour spike (in a sandbox) against a small sample of your prompt set after the deep-dive to validate time-to-first-byte and streaming behavior.
3) We'll share the pre-demo checklist and a region-by-region perf eligibility matrix prior to the call.

Attachments: pre-demo-checklist.md, SOC2-summary.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.
